AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/20/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 24.02.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Bonjemihary Colliery under Salanpur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its Bonjemihari 
Colliery (under Salanpur Area) in refusing / denying the Employment claim of Shri Mangal Marandi, dependent son 
of Late Nabin Marandi, Ex-Fitter, UM No. 157615, is just and legal? If not, to what relief Shri Mangal Marandi is 
entitled to?” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/20/2022-IR(CM-ID) dated 24.02.2022 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 
14.03.2022/01.07.2022 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing 
them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. General Secretary of Colliery Mazdoor Union (INTUC), representing the dependent son of Nabin Marandi 
submitted written statement on 16.08.2022. In brief, the fact giving rise to this Industrial Dispute is that Nabin 
Marandi was posted as Fitter at Bonjemihary Colliery, under Salanpur Aea of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter 
referred to as ECL). He died in harness on 31.10.2007, leaving behind Kolodi Marandi, his wife, Mangal Marandi, his 
son and one daughter. After the death of the employee, Kolodi Marandi claimed for employment against the death of 
her husband. After her proposal was turned down, she requested the management to keep the name of Mangal 
Marandi, her dependent son in the Live Roster and for payment of Monthly Monetary Cash Compensation 
(hereinafter referred to as MMCC) to her. Management claimed that as per Service Record of Nabin Marandi, the age 
of Mangal Marandi was 11 years at the time of death of the employee. In the written statement of the union, it is 
claimed that the assessment of age of Mangal Marandi was not done according to the medical jurisprudence. Initial 
Medical Examination (hereinafter referred to as IME) of Mangal Marandi was conducted on 11.06.2010 where his 
age was assessed between 13 and 16 years. According to the management the age of the dependent son was 11 years, 
10 months and 19 days on the date of death of his father. As he was under age, management did not maintain his 
name in the Live Roster of the company. Union claimed that according to the Birth Registration Certificate of Mangal 
Marandi, issued by the Government of West Bengal, his date of birth is 17.04.1995. In the School Admission 
Register the date of birth of Mangal Marandi is recorded as 17.04.1995 ad in the Admit Card issued by the West 
Bengal Board of Secondary Education (hereinafter referred to as WBBSE) the date of birth of the dependent son was 
also recorded as 17.04.1995. The IME did not take into consideration the statutory certificate and did not inform the 
result of the assessment of age of Mangal Marandi, as such no appeal could be preferred against determination of age 


3374 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 25, 2026/VAISAKHA 5, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


of the dependent through the Apex Medical Board of the company. This Industrial Dispute has been raised on behalf 
of the dependent son of the deceased employee claiming employment as per provisions of National Coal Wage 
Agreement (hereinafter referred to as NCWA). 


3: Management contested the case by filing written statement on 22.03.2023. The specific case of the 
management is that after death of Nabin Marandi his wife Kolodi Marandi claimed employment but the same was 
turned down on the ground that she had crossed the upper age limit. Thereafter, the wife of the deceased employee 
requested the management to keep the name of the Mangal Marandi in the Live Roster of the company as he was a 
minor at the time of death of his father. The employer company stated that the age of the dependent should be above 
12 years on the date of death of the employee for inclusion of the name of minor in the Live Roster. It is further stated 
that as per Form PS-3, the form related to family particulars of the employee, the age of Mangal Marandi at the time 
of death of his father was 11 years. On 11.06.2010 his age was assessed between 13 and 16 years and the age of the 
dependent son was computed as 11 years 10 months and 19 days on the date of death of his father. Management 
asserted that according to the rules of the company any party aggrieved with the decision of the IME Board could 
prefer an appeal within one month for further assessment by the Apex Medical Board. In the instant case no appeal 
was preferred against the findings of the IME Board as such the management regretted employee of the dependent 
and the name of Mangal Marandi was not maintained in the Live Roster. Further case of the management is that 
compassionate employment cannot be claimed as a matter of right and the case cannot be reconsidered after long 
lapse of time. The management further urged that MMCC was offered to the wife of the deceased employee in lieu of 
employment. It is contended that the management has rightly rejected the prayer for employment of Mangal Marandi 
as the terms for providing employment have to be strictly followed. Before conclusion, the management denied that it 
did not consider the document produced by the claimant for employment on compassionate ground and urged that the 
management is fully justified in refusing the employment. 


4. The issue which arose for consideration is whether the action of the management in refusing 
employment to Mangal Marandi is just and legal? If not, to what relief Mangal Marandi is entitled to. 


5. Union has examined Mangal Marandi as Workman Witness No. 1. He has filed an affidavit-in-chief wherein 
he stated that he submitted his Birth Certificate and School Certificate where his date of birth has been recorded. The 
witness further averred that no information has been given to him regarding the age assessed by IME Board and it was 
not possible for him to appeal or apply for holding assessment by Apex Medical Board. The witness stated that he has 
already crossed the age of 18 years and claimed employment as a dependent. In course of evidence following 
documents is produced by WW-1: 


(i) Copy of the Death Registration Certificate of Nabin Marandi is produced as Exhibit W-1. 
(ii) Copy of Birth Registration Certificate of Mangal Marandi is produced as Exhibit W-2. 
(iii) Copy of the Service Record Excerpt of Nabin Marandi is admitted as Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) Copy of the Note Sheet dated 02.01.2018 issued by the Dy. Manager (P), Bonjemihary Colliery, as 
Exhibit W-4. 


6. In course of cross-examination the witness deposed that he has filed his Registration Certificate, Admit Card, 
and Mark Sheet issued by WBBSE. Copy of the same have been produced as Exhibit W-5, W-6, and W-7 
respectively. Copy of IME declaration has been filed as Exhibit W-8 and M-2 and copy of the IME Report of Mangal 
Marandi is produced as Exhibit M-1. Witness claimed that at the time of death of his father he was more than 12 years 
of age. He denied the suggestion of the ECL management that at the time of death of his father he was less than 12 
years of age. 


7. Mr. Amitava Chakraborty, Manager (Personnel), Bonjemihary Colliery has been examined as Management 
Witness No. 1. He filed his affidavit-in-chief and stated that as per Form PS-3 the age of Mangal Marandi at the time 
of death of his father was 11 years. During IME of Mangal Marandi on 11.06.2010 his age was assessed between 13 
and 16 years and on the basis of such assessment the age of the dependent son is 11 years 10 months and 19 days on 
the date of death of his father. The management witness stated that the time limit for preferring an appeal against the 
findings of IME Board is one month and after lapse of such time no Apex Medical Board could consider any dispute 
regarding age. As the age of Mangal Marandi was less than 12 years, the management regretted his claim for 
maintaining his name in the Live Roster. Further assertion of the management is that compassionate employment 
cannot be claimed as a matter of right after long time has passed. Management claimed that MMCC was offered to 
the widow in lieu of employment but Kolodi Marandi did not accept the same. In course of evidence management 
witness produced the following documents : 


(i) Copy of the IME declaration of Mangal Marandi has been produced as Exhibit M-1/1. 
(ii) Copy of the IME Report of Mangal Marandi, as Exhibit M-2/1. 
(iii) Copy of Birth Registration Certificate of Mangal Marandi, as Exhibit M-3. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(1)] भारत का राजपत्र : अप्रैल 25, 2026/वैशाख 5, 1948 3375 


8. In course of cross-examination the management witness deposed that in Note Sheet dated 02.01.2018 
(Exhibit W-4) the Agent and Dy. Manager (P) of Bonjemihary Colliery, in Point No. 3 mentioned that the age of 
Mangal Marandi at the time of death of his father was 12 years 6 months and 14 days, as per Birth Certificate and 11 
years 5 months, as per Form PS-3. The witness also admitted that in Exhibit M-1 i.e., IME Report it considered the 
date of birth of Mangal Marandi as 17.04.1995 which implies that he was more than 12 years of age on 31.10.2007. 
The witness however denied that the dependent son is eligible for employment as per provisions of NCWA. 


9. Mr. Chandi Banerjee, union representative advancing his argument on behalf of the dependent son submitted 
that at the time of age assessment by the IME Board the candidate, Mangal Marandi disclosed his date of birth as 
17.04.1995, as per his Birth Registration Certificate. A copy of the Brith Registration Certificate issued by the 
Government of West Bengal under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 has been admitted as Exhibit W-2. 
Mr. Banerjee urged that according to the age of Mangal Marandi recorded in the Registration Certificate as well as 
Admit Card issued by WBBSE (Exhibit W-5 and W-6 respectively) it would appear that his date of birth has been 
consistently recorded as 17" day of April, 1995. Therefore, the management should have taken into consideration the 
date of birth of Mangal Marandi, appearing in the statutory documents as 17.04.1995, which will prevail over the age 
assessed by the IME Board, based upon approximation and not real. Mr. Banerjee argued that dependent son who was 
above 12 years of age in October 2007 is entitled to employment on the basis of the right subsisting in his favour 
under the provisions of NCWA. It is urged that the management should have treated the date of birth of the candidate 
appearing in the Birth Registration Certificate, and Admit Card of Madhyamik Examination as his actual date of birth. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate in reply argued that the death of Nabin Marandi took place in the year 2007 
when his son Mangal Marandi was below 12 years of age. After considering the prayer for maintaining the name of 
the dependent son in the Live Roster he was examined by the IME Board where his age was assessed as 13 to 16 
years and by implication the dependent son was 11 years 10 months and 19 days on the date of death of his father. 
Therefore, he was not eligible for his name to be maintained in the Live Roster as per provisions of NCWA. It is 
urged that management has committed no illegality by not granting employment to Mangal Marandi and the Industrial 
Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


11. I have considered the argument advanced on behalf of the management and union in the light of facts 
disclosed in their pleadings and evidence adduced. The admitted facts in this case are that Nabin Marandi was an 
employee of ECL and he died in harness on 31.10.2007. The dependent wife Kolodi Marandi was not provided with 
employment on the ground that she had exceeded the upper age limit. It also transpires from the written statement of 
the management that Kolodi Marandi requested the employer company to maintain the name of her son Mangal 
Marandi in the Live Roster. In this case union has produced a copy of Birth Registration Certificate of the dependent 
son as Exhibit W-2. It appears from the Birth Registration Certificate issued under the Registration of Births and 
Deaths Act, 1969 that the date of birth of Mangal Marandi is 17.04.1995. The certificate was issued from Kulti 
Municipality on 31.12.2002 1.6., prior to the death of Nabin Marandi and at the relevant time no question cropped up 
for providing employment to the dependent son in December 2002. No objection has been raised by the management 
at the time of admission of the document in evidence. Therefore, I have no doubt in my mind that the date of birth of 
Mangal Marandi recorded as 17.04.1995 is genuine. The Service Record Excerpt of Nabin Marandi (Exhibit W-3) 
was prepared in the year 1987. Therefore, it is obvious that the name of Mangal Marandi did not appear in that 
document as he was born in the year 1995. Management of ECL has claimed that as per the contents of Form PS-3, 
regarding family particulars of deceased employee, age of Mangal Marandi was computed as 11 years at the time of 
death of his father. It may be noted herein that the management has not produced Form PS-3 for consideration of this 
Tribunal and therefore the management of ECL cannot be permitted to rely upon the entries in Form PS-3 for 
determining the age of Mangal Marandi. In the absence of such a document no reliance can be placed upon entries 
made in such documents to hold that on the date of death of Nabin Marandi his minor son was 11 years of age. 


12. On the basis of the prayer made by the widow of the deceased an IME was held on 11.06.2010. It may be 
gathered from the application form filled up for the purpose of medical examination, which is produced as Exhibit W- 
8/M-2, that the date of birth of the dependent son was recorded as 17.04.1995. The IME Boad instead of considering 
the statutory document, which is going to represent the date of birth of Mangal Marandi in his future life for rest of 
the time, assess the age based upon his appearance which is not tenable. It appears from the report of IME (Exhibit 
M-1), that the Board members did not follow any scientific procedure or examination for the purpose of determining 
the age. The Board recorded the age of the person as 15 years as stated by the candidate and assessed the age of the 
person as 13 to 16 years on the basis of his appearance. If the recorded date of birth in the Birth Registration 
Certificate is presumed to be true then the age disclosed by Mangal Marandi before the IME Board is consistent and 
correct. The Admit Card issued by WBBSE in favour of Mangal Marandi also bears the same date of birth which is 
17.04.1995. therefore, the age recorded by the IME Board on the basis of appearance of a person does not have any 
scientific or legal basis and cannot have any application for the purpose of discarding his name from the Live Roster. 


13. Management claimed that no appeal was preferred by the family of the deceased employee against the age 
assessed by IME Board within 1 month from the date of holding IME. There is no trace of evidence in this case to 
establish that the management had communicated the outcome of IME to the family of the deceased employee within 
one month from the date of such assessment made by them on 11.06.2010. 


3376 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 25, 2026/VAISAKHA 5, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


14. From the aforesaid discussion and the evidence adduced by the parties in this case, it is abundantly clear that 
the management of employer company has deliberately delayed in finalizing the claim for employment of the 
dependent son 


on the basis of valid and legal evidence which tilts in favour of dependent son. According to the provisions of Clause 
9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-VIIL, if the dependent son is above the age of 12 years on the date of death of employee, then his 
name will be kept in the Live Roster and would be provided employment commensurate with his skill and 
qualifications when he attains the age of 18 years. In the present case as per the date of birth available in the Birth 
Registration Certificate issued by a public office Mangal Marandi was 12 years, 6 months, 14 days at the time of 
death of his father. Therefore, he was above 12 years of age and accordingly was entitled to be maintained in the Live 
Roster for his employment as per terms of settlement, binding the employer company and its employees through 
NCWA. I therefore, hold that Mangal Marandi is entitled to employment as a dependent of Nabin Marandi. Erroneous 
decision of the management has already delayed the employment procedure and it cannot be allowed to derive any 
benefit for their own acts. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Bonjemihary Colliery under 
Salanpur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. Management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to reconsider the 
claim for employment of Mangal Marandi as per the provisions of Clause 9.5.0 (iii) of National Coal Wage 
Agreement - VIII, treating 17.04.1995 as his date of birth, reflected in the Birth Registration Certificate. The 
procedure for employment must be completed within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. 
Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry 
of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/103/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 07.12.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the

SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of Jhanjra Project Colliery 1 & 2 Incline, Jhanjra Area, M/s. 
E.C.Ltd. not fixation the pay properly in the regularized post of Mining Sirdar-cum-Shot Firer to Sri Arjun 
Kuswaha is justified or not? If not, what relief the workman is entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/103/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 07.12.2022 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 08.12.2022 and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Arjun Kuswaha, the aggrieved workman filed written statement through Mr. Bipul Banerjee, learned 
advocate on 18.04.2023. A brief profile of the workman’s case is that he is a permanent employee of Eastern 
Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL) and was initially posted as SDL Operator. After passing the 
Mining Sirdarship course examination he was posted as Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer (Trainee) for a period of six 
months vide letter No. GM/JNR/PERS/2014/1234 dated 10/11.11.2014. On successful completion of the Training 
period the workman was regularized to the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer vide letter No. 
GM/JNR/PERS/2015/1094 dated 30/31.10.2015 but the pay which was fixed after his posting as Mining Sirdar -cum- 
Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ was less than the wages he was receiving as SDL Operator during 
the training period. According to the workman his Basic Pay as SDL Operator was Rs.52,536.30/- per month but 
while fixing his pay in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ his Basic Pay was reduced to Rs.51,006.12/- per month. It 
is contended that while fixing his pay the management of employer company did not consider the difference in Basic 
Pay. Several representations were made by the workman for restoration of Basic Pay to Rs.52,536.30/- per month 
with retrospective effect but the management denied his legitimate claim. It is the case of the workman that the 
management has acted in an illegal and unjust manner by not fixing his pay properly and he is entitled to a Basic Pay 
of Rs.52,536.30/- per month, from the time of his regularization in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer. 


3. Management of ECL contested the case by filing their written statement on 18.04.2023. The counter case of 
the management is that the management granted pay protection to the workman as per rules and no illegality has been 
committed in the matter of fixation of pay. It is asserted that the management is totally justified in fixing the pay of 
workman in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ as per guidelines of the 
company. 


4. The point for consideration is whether the action of the management in fixing the pay of the workman on 
regularization to the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer is legal and justified. If not, what relief the workman is 
entitled to. 


5. In order to establish his case, the workman examined himself as Workman Witness No. 1. He filed an 
affidavit-in-chief reiterating the facts of the case discharged in written statement. In course of his examination the 
workman has produced the following documents : 


(i) Copy of order dated 10/11.11.2014, whereby Arjun Kuswaha was asked to report to the Agent, 
Jhanjra Project Colliery for assignment of duty after completing Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer 
training, has been produced as Exhibit W-1. 


(ii) Copy of Charge Assumption Report dated 31.12.2014 of Arjun Kuswaha for reporting as Mining 
Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer, as Exhibit W-2. 

(iii) Copy of Office Order dated 30/31.10.2015 issued by the Area Personnel Manager, Jhanjra Area, 
whereby it was ordered that new Basic Pay would be fixed as per norms of the company and that 


Arjun Kuswaha was regularized in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer w.e.f. 25.05.2015, as 
Exhibit W-3.

(iv) Copy of Pay Slips of September, 2015 and October, 2015, where Basic Pay of Arjun Kuswaha was 
Rs.23,361.26/- and Rs 24,259.77/- respectively, as Exhibit W-4. 


(v) Copy of Pay Slip of November, 2015 and December, 2015, where Basic Pay of Arjun Kuswaha was 
Rs.21,492.36/- and Rs.22,279.72/- respectively, as Exhibit W-5. 


It transpires from the evidence that he was regularized in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in October, 2015. 
After completion of training period of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer he was asked to report before the Agent, 
Jhanjra Project Colliery for assignment of duty and assumed charge as Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer on 31.12.2014. 
Copies of Pay slip of September, 2015 and October, 2015 have been produced which show that his Basic Pay was 
Rs.23,361.26/- and Rs.24,259.77/- respectively. Copies of Pay Slips of November, 2015 and December, 
2015 have been admitted in the evidence as Exhibit W-5. It appears from the document that the Basic pay in the 
month of November, 2015 and December, 2015, was reduced to Rs.21,492.36/- and Rs.22,279.72/- respectively. 


6. In cross-examination it was suggested on behalf of the management that the workman was not entitled to any 
higher pay after his regularization to a higher post than a General Mazdoor, which the witness denied. 


7. Management examined Mr. Alaric Oneal Lyndem as Management Witness No. 1. He has filed an affidavit- 
in-chief where he stated that after successful completion of training period of six months, Arjun Kuswaha was 
regularized as a Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ as per guidelines of the 
company and his Pay was fixed in monthly rated category. The management however denied that the fixation of pay 
of the concerned workman in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ was done in an illegal manner. The witness stated 
that the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ is an entry level mining 
supervisory post which is done through selection and not by promotion and his Basic was not affected when he was 
converted from daily rated to monthly rated employee. The witness during his examination produced the following 
documents : 


(i) Copy of order dated 10/11.11.2014, whereby Arjun Kuswaha was asked to report to the Agent, 
Jhanjra Project Colliery for assignment of duty after completing Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer 
training has been produced as Exhibit M-1. 


(ii) Copy of Office Order dated 30/31.10.2015 issued by the Area Personnel Manager, Jhanjra Area, 
whereby it was ordered that new Basic would be fixed as per norms of the company and that Arjun 
Kuswaha was regularized in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer w.e.f. 25.05.2015, as 
Exhibit M-2. 


(iii) Copy of the Guidelines for promotion dated 04.10.2012, as Exhibit M-3. 


In his evidence the management witness failed to produce the order of pay fixation in respect of Arjun Kuswaha. He 
admitted that in his affidavit-in-chief that the statement prepared by the System Officer does not bear any reference 
number nor any seal or signature of the authority. Witness deposed that while the workman was posted as SDL 
Operator, his Basic Pay was Rs.23,361.26/-. The witness further stated that the claim of the workman that he has not 
been paid proper wages is incorrect. He also deposed that the annual increment of the workman is three percent (3%) 
of his Basic. 


8. In course of cross-examination the management witness deposed that at the time of posting as Mining Sirdar 
-cum- Shot Firer the Basic Pay of Arjun Kuswaha in the post of SDL Operator had already surpassed the minimum 
Basic Pay of a Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’. It may be gathered from the 
evidence of witness that minimum Basic Pay of Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ is Rs.19,035.02/- per month. 
According to the management Arjun Kuswaha was not promoted but was regularized to the new post. The witness 
denied that after regularization of Arjun Kuswaha as Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer his pay was reduced at the rate 
of one percent (1%) of Basic. 


9. Mr. Shabe Alam, union representative argued that Arjun Kuswaha completed the Mining Sirdarship course 
and underwent training for six months. During the period of his training for six months, he received difference of his 
Basic but on completion of his training he was regularized in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical 
and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ w.e.f. 25.05.2015 through Office Order 30/31.10.2015 (Exhibit W-3). It was provided that 
the new Basic would be fixed as per norms of the company by the Associated Finance. The management of the 
employer company however did not fix the pay in proper manner. It is argued that as per Implementation Instructions 
No. 23 and decision taken in the Standardization Meeting dated 23.01.1980, when an employee of a lower category 
temporarily works in the place of a higher category workman he should be paid an officiating allowance of ten 
percent (10%) of his total wages or the statutory pay of the higher category worker for whom he deputizes, whichever 
is higher and where an employee in a lower category works in the place of a workman of higher category, he should 
be entitled to payment of officiating allowance which shall be the difference between his wage and the minimum of 
the higher category, if such minimum is higher than his existing pay. In case, by this method of adjustment, he gets 
less than one increment in the officiating scale, he should be given one increment in that scale. In the event of the

existing pay of the officiating workman being higher than the minimum of the scale of pay of the higher category in 
which he works, then his existing pay should be adjusted into the next higher step in the higher category's scale and he 
should be given one increment in that scale. Mr. Alam argued that the workman was a daily wager receiving 
Rs.898.51/- per day and on working for twenty-six (26) days his Basic Pay reached Rs.23,361.26/- per month. After 
the workman was regularized to the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer w.e.f. 25.05.2015 his Basic Pay was fixed 
by multiplying his daily wages by number of working days. Referring to Exhibit W-4, which is a Pay Slip for the 
month of September, 2015 it is argued that the pay of workman was simply converted from daily rate to monthly rate 
after his regularization to a higher category and he did not receive the amount which he was receiving during his 
training period as difference of wages. Union representative argued that on regularization the workman is also entitled 
to an increment of three percent (3%) of Basic Pay as on 25.05.2015. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate argued that by Office Order dated 30/31.10.2015 (Exhibit W-3/M-2) 
Arjun Kuswaha, SDL Operator, U. M. No. 122213 of 1 and 2 Incline, Jhanjra Project Colliery, having successfully 
completed the training on 24.05.2015 has been regularized in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical 
and Supervisor Grade ‘C’ but the same is not to be considered as promotion and he was only entitled to the initial 
Basic of a Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer. It is submitted that the Industrial Dispute has no merit and the same is 
liable to be dismissed. 


11. I have considered the rival arguments in the light of the fact and circumstances of the case disclosed in the 
pleadings and evidence adduced by the parties. It is admitted that the workman was regularized to the post of Mining 
Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer as per Office Order dated 30/31.10.2015 (Exhibit W-3/M-2). From the Pay slip of September, 
2015 (Exhibit W-4) it appears that the Basic Pay of the workman was Rs.23,361.26/- on computing and consolidating 
the daily wages of Rs.898.51/- per day. After completion of the training period and regularization, the Pay of the 
workman was required to be fixed as a monthly rated worker. On perusal of Exhibit W-5, a Pay Slip of December, 
2015 it appears that the Basic Pay was fixed as Rs.22,279.72/- which is less than the Basic Pay of Rs.23,361.26/- 
which was being received by the workman before his regularization. From the averment of Management Witness No. 
1, it is gathered that the management is not inclined to grant any increment in the Basic Pay of the workman on his 
regularization to a higher post. On regularization of a workman in a higher post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer, the 
Basic Pay appears to be less than the Pay received by him in the lower category of SDL Operator. Therefore, 
according to the recommendation of the Standardization Meeting dated 23.01.1980, Arjun Kuswaha, the workman 
would be entitled to a Basic Pay with increment of three percent (3%) in the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer. 
Management of ECL is therefore required to pay one increment of three percent (3%) of minimum of the scale of pay 
of the higher category i.e., the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’, in 
which the workman was regularized from 25.05.2015. I therefore, hold that the management of ECL had failed to fix 
the pay of Arjun Kuswaha in proper manner. Management of ECL is directed to fix the Basic Pay of the concerned 
workman w.e.f. the day of his regularization i.e., 25.05.2015 and also pay his arrears of Basic Pay and Dearness 
Allowance within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of | & 2 Incline, Jhanjra Project 
Colliery under Jhanjra Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. Management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to 
fix the Basic Pay of Arjun Kuswaha by granting him one increment of three percent (3%) of minimum Basic Pay of 
the higher category i.e., the post of Mining Sirdar -cum- Shot Firer in Technical and Supervisor Grade ‘C’, in which 
the workman was regularized from 25.05.2015. Arrears of Pay and Allowance be disbursed to the workman within 
two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above 
findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for 
information and Notification.

SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management not to consider the application dated 27.12.2010 of Shri Tapan Hari 
for re-instatement as per Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007 as on the date of the application he

1. On receiving order No. L-22012/122/2013—CIR)(CM-ID) dated 18.09.2013 this reference case No.14 of 2013 
was registered on 14.02.2024 and an order passed to issuing notice to the parties through registered post for

2. Mr. Niren Chandra Das, Organizing Secretary, Colliery Mazdoor Republican Sabha (BMM) filed written 
statement on behalf of Tapan Hari on 02.08.2014. The fact in brief is that Tapan Hari was appointed as a General

3. Workman contended that no notice of enquiry was served upon him before holding ex-parte domestic 
enquiry. The workman had no opportunity to defend his case. The union applied for re-instatement of the workman 
on the basis of Memorandum of Settlement reached which disclosed that if the workman was below the age of 45 
years and absented for less than 9 (nine) months, management would re-instate the workman in his service. It is 
claimed that the management issued a charge-sheet on 11.02.1992 but in the written statement it is disclosed that the 
workman remained absent from duty from 04.08.1990 to 12.03.1992. According to the workman his dismissal was 
illegal and the management should be directed to re-instate the workman in his service with payment of back wages. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अप्रैल 25, 2026/वैशाख 5, 1948 3381 


4. Management has not filed any written statement in this case. Initially the case was fixed for ex-parte hearing 
on 07.10.2015. At a later stage, Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate appeared for the management without filing any 
Vokalatnama. 


5. The moot point for consideration in this case is whether the action of the management in not considering the 
application dated 27.12.2010 submitted by Tapan Hari for his re-instatement as per Memorandum of Settlement dated 
22.05.2007 is legal and the punishment of dismissal on the ground of absenteeism is fair and proportionate. 


6. Tapan Hari adduced evidence by filing affidavit. In his cross-examination by the management, the workman 
witness No.1(Tapan Hari) deposed that he does not remember his date of birth but he was born in the year 1968. He 
further deposed that his service particulars are entered in the ‘B’ Form Register of ECL. He has no document to 
prove his date of birth. The witness admitted that he was absent from duty for nearly 6(six) years and had no reason 
for his absence. The witness further deposed that he did not attend duty on his own desire and wish. A departmental 
proceeding was started and he was dismissed. The witness was re-examined or re-called and he produced a copy of 
application dated 27.12.2010 (marked as Exhibit W-1) where he prayed for re-instatement as per the Terms of 
Memorandum of Settlement. Witness failed to produce any document in support of his absence for nearly 2(two) 
years as mentioned in the charge-sheet and also did not submit any application before the management of the 
company praying for re-instatement. 


7. Management without filing Vokalatnama as well as written statement, has adduced evidence through Mr. 
Sanjib Kumar Ghosh as management witness. The statements made by the management witness on affidavit is 
considered for ends of justice. The witness stated in affidavit that workman was absent from 04.08.1990 and charge- 
sheet was issued to him on 11.02.1992 for his unauthorized absence without any sanctioned leave or prior permission 
from the management. The management witness deposed that the charge-sheet was sent to his home address but the 
Ex-workman failed to submit any satisfactory reply for which domestic enquiry was started. Notice of enquiry was 
issued and ex-parte enquiry was held. On the basis of findings of the Enquiry Officer the workman was found guilty 
of the charge and the Disciplinary Authority dismissed the workman from service on 30.03.1992. 


Management witness at the time of adducing evidence produced the following documents. 
1. Copy of charge-sheet dated 11.02.1992is produced as Exhibit M-1. 
Copy of notice for Domestic Enquiry to Tapan Hari as Exhibit M-2. 


Copy of letter appointing Enquiry Officer for domestic enquiry as Exhibit M-3. 


2 
3 
4. Copy of enquiry proceedings in 4 (four) pages is marked as Exhibit M-4. 
5. Copy of findings of Enquiry Officer as Exhibit M-S. 

6 


Copy of the order of dismissal of the workman as Exhibit M-6. 
7. Copy of the order of dismissal communicated to the workman as Exhibit M-7. 


8. Mr. Milan Kumar Bandyopadhyay, learned advocate for the union argued that the only contention of the 
union is that the concerned workman has been dismissed from his service under ECL without any information about 
holding departmental proceeding and no notice was served. It is argued that after dismissal of the workman on the 
basis of ex-parte proceedings, the workman made a representation before the management on 27.12.2010 which is 
produced as Exhibit W-1 but management did not consider his application for re-instatement in service in Terms of 
Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007. 


9. Learned advocate for the union argued that as per Terms of Settlement dated 22.05.2007 a dismissed 
workman who is below the age of 45 years and have remained absent for less than 9 (nine) months is entitled to be re- 
instated in a service to ECL. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management in reply argued that the workman was a habitual 
absentee and he remained absent for more than one year without any authorization or information to the employer 
company. Furthermore, the workman made no representation before the management for his re-instatement for re- 
consideration after the order of dismissal was passed against him on 30.03.1992 (Exhibit M-6). After eighteen years 
the workman filed an application for reinstatement. 


11. I have considered the rival arguments advanced by learned advocates for the union and the management. 
From the evidence on record, I find that Tapan Hari was absent from his duty on 04.08.1990 and charge-sheet was 
issued on 11.02.1992. The period of unauthorized absence of the workman was for one year and 6(six) months till the 
issuance of charge-sheet. The workman in his evidence in-chief however admitted that he was absent from duty for 
nearly 6 (six) years. No cogent reason has been assigned for his absence from duty. I find from the record that before 
initiating the domestic enquiry notice of enquiry was issued to the workman (Exhibit M-2). A departmental enquiry 
was held by Sri A. Ghosh, Dy. Personnel Manager, Benalee Colliery and the enquiry proceedings has been produced 


3382 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 25, 2026/VAISAKHA 5, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


as Exhibit M-4. The Report of Enquiry in original has been produced as Exhibit M-5. The report revealed that the 
charge of unauthorized absence under Clause 17(i)(n) of the Model Standing Order has been well established against 
the workman and he was punished by way of dismissal from service. I find no illegality in the act of dismissing an 
employee who remains absent for a long period. 


12. According to the Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007 management of ECL agreed to re- 
instate those employees who were dismissed for the reason of absenting for a period below nine months and were 
below 45 years of age and also agreed that such cases would be considered on merit basis. In the present case the 
workman has not fulfilled the require conditions enshrined in point No.7 of the Memorandum of Settlement dated 
22.05.2007. He was admittedly absent for more than nine months without information. Therefore, he did not fulfill 
the condition in the Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007, for his re-instatement in service. Accordingly, 
there is no merit in the case and the workman is not entitled in any relief. 


Hence, 
ORDER 


The Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. The workman is not entitled to any relief. The 
management has committed no illegality by not considering his application dated 27.12.2010 for re-instatement as he 
did not fulfill one of the conditions for being considered. Let an award be drawn up on the basis of my above 
findings.

that promotion was not granted to Ranjit Kumar Banerjee on the basis of his I.T.I./N.C.V.T. certificate.

6. Considering the arguments advanced by learned advocate for ECL as well as the evidence record together

to the necessity and vacancy of the employer company. The workman has already retired from service in the year 
2013 and he is not entitled to any benefit. No evidence has been adduced on behalf of remaining 08(eight) workmen 
who were included in the Industrial Dispute. Therefore, other workmen have failed to establish their claim against the 
management. The Industrial Dispute is accordingly dismissed on contest.

SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the management of Jambad Colliery, Kajora Area, M/s. E.C.Ltd. in not providing 
employment to Sri Panchu Kole is justified? If not, what relief the dependent Sri Panchu Kole son of Late 
Sanichar Kole is entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. 1(41)/2023/E dated 23.11.2023 from the Office of the Deputy Chief Labour 
Commissioner (Central), Asansol, Ministry of Labour, Government of India, for adjudication of the dispute a 
Reference case was registered on 04.12.2023 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through 
registered post, directing them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support 
of their claims. 


2: Panchu Kole filed written statement on 19.01.2024 in support of his claim for employment as dependent. 
Fact of the case as disclosed in the written statement is that Sanichar Kole was employed as a Masson at Jambad 
Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL), who died in harness on 
18.11.1993. Panchu Kole, the dependent son of the deceased employee submitted an application on 06.03.1995, 
claiming employment as a dependent. In the Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007 it was agreed that the 
employment cases prior to 01.07.1996 will be considered by the management. After initial medical examination and 
screening of Panchu Kole at Colliery and Area level, the employment file was sent to the ECL Headquarters. As per 
letter No. ECL/JC/C-6/P&IR/2016-17/49/469 dated 12/14.03.2017 Panchu Kole was advised to appear before the 
General Manager (Personnel), ECL, along with some more documents. No information was given to the incumbent 
regarding the fate of his application and finally the present Industrial Dispute has been raised. According to the 
workman Clause 9.5.0(iii) of National Coal Wage Agreement-V (hereinafter referred to as NCWA-V) provides : 


“ In case of death either in mine accident or for other reasons or medical unfitness under clause 9.4.0, if no 
employment has been offered and the male dependant of the concerned worker is fifteen (15) years and above in age 
he will be kept on a live roster and would be provided employment commensurate with his skill and qualifications 
when he attains the age of eighteen (18) years. During the period the male dependant is on live roster, the female 
dependant will be paid monetary compensation as per rates at paras (i) & (ii) above.” 


Therefore, the name of the dependent son should have been maintained in the Live Roster and employment should be 
provided on his attaining the age of eighteen years. In the instant case Initial Medical Examination (hereinafter 
referred to as IME) of Panchu Kole was held on 16.07.1999 after lapse of four years. The management did not offer 
any Monthly Monetary Cash Compensation (hereinafter referred to as MMCC) to the wife of the deceased and the 
name of Panchu Kole was not maintained in the Live Roster. During conciliation proceeding the management claimed 
that mother of Panchu Kole was an employee of the company and nowhere in the NCWA it was mentioned that if the 
mother of the dependent in an employee of the company, the dependent of the deceased employee will not get 
employment under the company. According to the petitioner, management has deliberately violated the provisions of 
NCWA. It is admitted that Smt. Jiria Kole, wife of Sanichar Kole was an employee of Parascole Colliery under 
Kunustoria Area of ECL. The union prayed that the management may be directed to provide employment to the 
dependent without further delay and compensation for the delay caused. 


3. Management contested the Reference case by filing their written statement on 16.04.2024. It is contended 
inter-alia that Clause 3.6(iii) of Implementation Instruction No. 8 (hereinafter referred to as 1.1. No. 8) under NCWA-

“In case of death either in mine accident or for other reasons or medical unfitness under Clause 9.4.0 (NCWA- V), if 
no employment has been offered and the male dependant of the concerned worker is 15 years and above in age he 
will be kept on a live roster and would be provided employment commensurate with his skill and qualifications when 
he attains the age of 18 years. During the period the male dependant is on live roster, the female dependant will be 
paid monetary compensation” 


It is further stated that the Chief Personnel Manager (IR), Coal India Limited issued a clarification dated 
14/16.10.2003 bearing Ref. No. CIL/C-5B/JBCCI/194, which reads as follows :

“ THE PROVISION TO KEEP NAME OF MINOR DEPENDANT IN THE LIVE ROSTER FOR THE PURPOSE OF 
EMPLOYMENT UNDER CLAUSE 9.4.0 OF NCWA-V, AS PER PARA 3.6(III) OF THIS OFFICE 
IMPLEMENTATION INSTRUCTION NO.8 OF NCWA-V CIRCULATED VIDE NO. CIL/JBCCI-V/LI.NO.(8/96 /2627 
DATED 22.2.1996 IS EFFECTIVE FROM THE DATE OF ISSUE OF THE ORDER L.E., 22.2.1996.” 

Management contended that Panchu Kole was examined by the IME Board and his age was assessed as 20 to 25 years

7. In course of cross-examination the management witness deposed that the provision for maintaining the name

8. Heard the argument advanced by Mr. Milan Kumar Bandyopadhyay, learned advocate for the dependent son. 
It is argued that the management has not provided employment to the dependent son as per provisions of NCWA-V,

9. Mr. Sayantan Mukherjee, learned advocate for the management, in reply argued that though NCWA-V was 
made applicable during the period from 01.07.1991 to 30.06.1996, but as per Circular bearing Ref. No. CIL:JBCCI- 
V:LI.No.(8/96)/2627 dated 22.02.1996, the provision to keep the name of the minor dependent in the Live Roster for 
the purpose of providing employment under of NCWA-V was made effective from the date of issuance of the Order 
i.e., 22.02.1996 and the petitioner is not entitled to any employment. 


10. Having considered the arguments advanced by the learned advocates for the respective parties and the 
materials on record along with various provisions of NCWA-V and Circular dated 22.02.1996, I am of the considered 
view that Panchu Kole, son of the deceased employee was a minor at the time of death of his father on 18.11.1993. 
Though other provisions of NCWA-V were made applicable and binding w.e.f. 01.07.1991 to 30.06.1996, the 
expressed provision of Circular dated 22.02.1996 made it clear that the provision related to maintaining the names of 
minor dependents in the Live Roster of the company for the purpose of employment on attaining majority, in the case 
of death of employment would be apply only from the date of issuance of I.I. No. 8 dated 22.02.1996. Therefore, the 
claim for employment of Panchu Kole cannot be entertained under the provisions of NCWA. The management of 
Jambad Colliery therefore did not controvert any provision of NCWA by not allowing the prayer for employment of 
the dependent son. 


11. It is gathered from the evidence of the petitioner that his mother Jiria Kole was an employee of ECL at 
Parascole Colliery under Kunustoria Area and she died on 21.07.1996, therefore there is no justification in the claim 
for MMCC at this stage. Accordingly, I hold that the present Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed on contest. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest against Panchu Kole, son of Late Sanichar Kole, ex- 
employee of Eastern Coalfields Limited. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the 
Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and 
Notification.

In exercise of powers conferred under sub-section (5) of Section 12 read with sub-section (2A) of Section 10 
of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Ministry of Labour, Government of India through the Office of 
the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), New Delhi, vide its Order No. 24(42)/2024-IR dated 18.12.2024 has been 
pleased to refer the following dispute between the employer, i.e., (1) Chairman-cum-Managing Director, ECL, 
Sanctoria and (2) General Manager, Satgram Sripur Area, ECL and Secretary, Colliery Mazdoor Union (INTUC) for 
adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of Eastern Coalfields Limited in merging Sripur Area with Satgram 
Area is justified? If not, what relief the employee of Sripur Area is entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. 24(42)/2024-IR dated 18.12.2024 from the Office of the Chief Labour 
Commissioner (Central), New Delhi, Ministry of Labour, Government of India, for adjudication of the dispute a 
Reference case was registered on 23.12.2024 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through 
registered post, directing them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support 
of their claims. 


2. Union filed written statement on 19.08.2025 stating therein that Sripur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as ECL) was merged with Satgram Area of ECL vide Order No. ECL/C- 
5(D)/Min/1041363/EE/1031 dated 31.03.2023 issued by Mr. Subrata Dasgupta, Deputy General Manager (P/EE), 
ECL, Headquarters, Sanctoria. The Office Order was circulated on ‘WhatsApp’ and no hard copy of the same is 
provided to the Department of erstwhile Sripur Area nor to the central trade union of the Area. According to the union 
out of fourteen (14) Areas, Works Committees at Area level were not discussed by the management about such 
merger. Therefore, Works Committees functioning in different forums of Area level as Area JCC, Area Welfare 
Board, Area Tripartite committee, etc. were not informed. The entire erstwhile committee of Sripur Area was 
abolished. The order of merger has leading to unfair labour practice under Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The union 
further contended that in majority number of cases unions were party to the agreement along with management of 
erstwhile Sripur Area and they have been badly affected due to the merger. The post of Area General Manager and 
Head of Departments have been amalgamated into one instead of two. The contract workers who are engaged as 
Driver of hired vehicles and erstwhile Sripur Area have lost their employment. The setup of Area Offices of erstwhile 
Sripur Area were shifted to Satgram. Due to merger of the two areas promotional scope of employees have been 
reduced due to Manpower Budget. Ex-employees of erstwhile Sripur Area are wandering for payment of their legal 
dues. Under such circumstances the union prayed to pass an order to set aside the unjustified order of the 
management, resulting in merger of Sripur Area with Satgram Area. 


3. Management has filed their written statement contending inter-alia that the dispute raised by the union does 
not constitute any Industrial Dispute and submitted that the merger of Sripur Area and Satgram Area w.e.f. 
01.04.2023 has been approved by ECFD of ECL on the 297 Meeting of 2022 and the said merger is the policy matter 
of the company which has come into existence vide Order No. ECL/C-5(D)/Min/1041363/EE/1031 dated 31.03.2023. 
A copy of the order has been annexed as Annexure-I. Management further contended that the service conditions of the 
employees on the roll of Satgram-Sripur Area have remained unaltered and the interest of employees has not been 
affected due to such merger, which is purely on administrative ground, for better functioning of the Mines under 
Satgram-Sripur Area and the union has no right to challenge the merger in any manner. Management asserted that the 
merger of Sripur and Satgram Areas is justified and the union is not entitled to get any relief. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अप्रैल 25, 2026/वैशाख 5, 1948 3389 


4. The case is fixed up today on the point of maintainability. Learned advocates appearing for the respective 
parties advanced their arguments, reiterating the stand taken by them in their pleadings. I have carefully considered 
the contention of the union and management’s argument, justifying the decision of merger of the two areas on the 
ground that it is an administrative policy of the company and does not affect the employees adversely in any manner. 


5. Section 2(k) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 has defined the terms “Industrial Dispute” : 


“ “industrial dispute" means any dispute or difference between employers and employers or between employers and 


workmen, or between workmen and workmen, which is connected with the employment or non-employment or the 
terms of employment or with the conditions of labour, of any person.” 


6. The union has expressed its grievance for not been consulted before the merger of the two Areas by the 
management on 31.03.2023. It appears from letter bearing No. ECL/CS/27 (Z-7)/29" of 2022/4 dated 30.11.2022 
that a meeting was held by the Empowered Committee of the Functional Directors of Eastern Coalfields Limited on 
21.11.2022 and after carrying out a detailed study, a report was placed by the Vigilance Department on merger of the 
Sripur and Satgram Areas, which was considered by the Secretary (Coal), Government of India on 10.01.2022. After 
detailed deliberation the empowered committee agreed to accept the Vigilance Department’s report on merger of two 
areas. The said decision was taken for the purpose of benefit of the company and effective deployment of manpower 
by abolition of key posts of one of the areas, giving rise to saving in POL to the tune of Rs. 0.47 crore and savings in 
hiring charges of vehicles at an estimated annual savings of Rs. 129.47 crore. 


7. In my considered view such benefits accruing to the employer company due to the merger would certainly 
benefit the management as well as union. Not a single case has been cited whereby an employee of the company has 
been adversely affected due to such decision. Therefore, there is no cause of action for the union to raise objection 
against the decision of the management merging two areas of ECL for administrative and financial benefits. The 
decision taken by the management is a prerogative of the management and the union has no locus standi to claim its 
participation in taking such decision. I therefore, hold that the Reference made as Industrial Dispute is not 
maintainable as it does not satisfy the test of Industrial Dispute and it does not disturb the terms of employment or the 
conditions of labours or any person. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. The Reference case is found not maintainable as it does 
not satisfy the test of Industrial Dispute. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the 
Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and 
Notification.

For the Management of ECL: Mr. P. K. Das, Advocate.

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/44/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 04.05.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Central Hospital at Kalla of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their workman for 
adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its Central Hospital, 
Kalla in non-payment/denial of payment of House Rent Allowance from the month of April, 2019 in respect 
of Shri Sourav Das, Physiotherapist, Central Hospital, Kalla, U.M. No. 135392 is just and legal? If not, to 
what relief the workman is entitled to? ” 


1 On receiving Order No. L-22012/44/2022-IR(CM-ID) dated 04.05.2022 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 04.05.2022 / 
01.07.2022 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear 
and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. The aggrieved workman filed written statement on 31.01.2023 through Mr. Bipul Banerjee, Advocate. Fact 
of the case in brief is that, Sourav Das is a permanent employee of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to 
as ECL) and he is presently posted as a Physiotherapist at Central Hospital, Kalla on his transfer from Jhanjra Project 
Colliery on 18.03.2019. The workman is resident of Laskarbandh, Natundanga, PO: Loudoha, Dist.: Paschim 
Bardhaman. His place of work is situated more than five kilometers away from his place of residence. According to 
the house allotment rules of the employer company, quarters are provided to the employees who are residing beyond 
five kilometers and if quarters are not provided by the company they are entitled to House Rent Allowance 
(hereinafter referred to as HRA) according to the provisions of National Coal Wage Agreement (hereinafter referred 
to as NCWA). According to the workman no quarters has been allotted to him due to which the workman had to make 
his own arrangement for accommodation at Asansol. He submitted an application dated 12.08.2020 requesting for 
cancellation of his prayer for allotment of quarters and further prayed for HRA as per rules of the company. The 
workman also submitted application dated 27.11.2019 and 07.04.2021, requesting for payment of HRA since his 
joining at Central Hospital, Kalla but the management has not paid him any HRA. 


3. Further case of the workman is that Office Order No. ECL/CHK/Quarter/2019/3162 dated 26.12.2019 has no 
application upon him. Furthermore, a common letter bearing No. ECL/CHK/Admn/2021/1340 dated 24/29.04.2021 
addressed to four other persons, informing that the representations made by them will be raised in the meeting of 
House Committee for allotment of quarters has no application upon him. It is disclosed in his written statement that 
the he was receiving HRA at the rate of Rs.525.86/- (Rupees five hundred twenty-five and eighty-six paise only) per 
month during his posting at Jhanjra Project Colliery and he is entitled to same on his joining Central Hospital at Kalla 
from April 2019 till date. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(1)] भारत का राजपत्र : अप्रैल 25, 2026/वैशाख 5, 1948 3391 


4. Management of Central Hospital at Kalla contested the Industrial Dispute by filing their written statement 
on 31.01.2023, wherein it is stated that the workman after joining Central Hospital at Kalla applied for allotment of 
quarters on 31.10.2019, stating that his residence at Laskarbandh was approximately fifty (50) Kilometers away from 
his place of work. According to the management, quarters is allotted to the employee as per record of the Housing 
Committee. A meeting of the Housing Committee was held on 17.12.2019 and the Housing Committee allotted 
Quarters No. NTD-4/4 to the workman as per his entitlement. The workman did not occupy the same and submitted 
an application on 12.06.2020, requesting for allotment of ‘A’ type Quarters. As per housing rules of the company, 
employees who are in the grade below Technical ‘C’ are entitled to NHS or below ‘A’ type quarters as such the 
concerned workman was entitled to allotment of NHS/NTD type quarters and not ‘A’ type Quarters. According to the 
guidelines of the company vide ECL/CMD/C-6E/10/621 dated 21.07.2012 issued by the General Manager (P&IR), 
ECL, employees refusing to occupy the allotted quarters or surrender the allotted quarters will not be eligible to draw 
HRA. The management asserted that the workman having refused to accept the allotted quarters is not entitled to 
any HRA. 

3: The moot question for consideration is whether the action of the management of ECL denying payment of 
HRA to Sourav Das, an employee of Central Hospital, Kalla from April, 2019 is justified? If not, to what relief the 
workman is entitled to. 


6. In order to establish the claim for HRA, Sourav Das has been examined as Workman Witness No. 1. He filed 
an affidavit-in-chief where he clearly stated that no quarters was allotted to him and by his letter dated 27.11.2019 he 
requested the management for payment of HRA. He further stated that on 12.06.2020 he submitted an application 
with a further request for allotment of quarters but the management did not take any action. When no quarters was 
allotted to him, he arranged for a rented accommodation at Asansol and submitted an application dated 12.08.2020 
for cancellation of his prayer for allotment of quarters. It appears from his averment in the affidavit-in-chief that the 
management informed him along with four others by letter bearing No. ECL/CHK/Admn/2021/1340 dated 
24/29.04.2021 that his representation will be raised in the meeting of the Housing Committee for allotment of 
quarters. It is also stated in the affidavit-in-chief that previously he was receiving HRA of Rs.525.86/- per month. The 
witness asserted that denial of HRA to him from April, 2019 is illegal and he is entitled to HRA. The witness 
produced the following documents : 
(i) Copy of application of Sourav Das dated 31.10.2019, praying for allotment of quarters is produced 
as Exhibit W-1. 
(ii) Copy of application of Sourav Das submitted on 27.11.2019 for payment of House Rent Allowance, 
as Exhibit W-2. 
(iii) Copy of application of Sourav Das dated 12.06.2020 addressed to the Personnel Manager, Central 
Hospital, Kalla, whereby he once again prayed for allotting ‘A’ type quarters, as Exhibit W-3. 
(iv) Copy of application of Sourav Das dated 12.08.2020 whereby he prayed for cancellation of his 
earlier application for allotment of company’s quarter, as Exhibit W-4. 
(v) Copy of letter dated 24/29.04.2021 issued by the CMO (Admn), Central Hospital, Kalla, informing 
Sourav Das that his representation for payment of HRA was forwarded to ECL Headquarters for 
approval, as Exhibit W-5). 
(vi) Copy of Pay slip for the month March, 2019, as Exhibit W-6. 
(vii) Copy of Pay slip for the month April, 2019, as Exhibit W-6/1. 
7. On cross-examination by the management, workman witness admitted that he heard that quarters were 
allotted to the employees of ECL after decision was taken by the Housing Committee of Central Hospital, Kalla. The 
workman witness was not confronted with the letter of allotment of quarters dated 26.12.2019 and he further deposed 
that despite submission of his application, the Housing Committee of Central Hospital, Kalla did not allot any 
quarters to him and no communication was made to him regarding allotment of quarters. 
8. Mr. Raj Narayan Bhattacharjee, Chief Manager (Pers), Central Hospital, Kalla is examined as Management 
Witness No. 1. In his affidavit-in-chief the witness stated that Sourav Das came on transfer to Central Hospital, Kalla 
on 18.03.2019. After joining he applied for allotment of quarters on 31.10.2019, stating that he was attending his 
work from his residential address at Laskarbandh which is 50 Kilometers from Central Hospital, Kalla. The witness 
stated that Sourav Das is not entitled to HRA as quarters was allotted to him by the management w.e.f. 26.12.2019. 
The witness produced the copy of application submitted by Sourav Das dated 31.10.2019 as Exhibit M-1 and a copy 
of Office Order dated 26.12.2019 showing allotment of Quarters No. NTD-4/4 at Central Hospital, Kalla in favour of 
Sourav Das as Exhibit M-2. The witness deposed that after quarters was allotted, Sourav Das submitted an application 
on 12.06.2020, praying for allotment of ‘A’ type Quarters to him on early basis which has been marked as Exhibit M- 
3. The witness deposed that Sourav Das was not eligible for ‘A’ type Quarters and no reply was given to his 
application. It transpires from his testimony that Sourav Das thereafter submitted an application dated 12.08.2020 
stating that since he had applied for the quarters one year earlier and no quarters was allotted to him, his prayer for 
allotment of quarters may be cancelled. The prayer for cancellation of quarters has been produced as Exhibit M-4. 
The witness produced a copy of letter dated 21.03.2009 issued by the General Manager (Admin/Welfare) addressed to 
CMO (I/C), Central Hospital, Kalla wherein it was communicated that the Director (Personnel), ECL in the 
35" meeting of Coal India Limited Welfare Board Meeting held on 21.04.2007 decided that payment of HRA may be 


3392 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 25, 2026/VAISAKHA 5, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


allowed in those mines / areas only where there is a shortage of quarters. HRA should not be paid if quarters are 
available, or allotted but are not accepted by the concerned employee. The copy of letter has been admitted in 
evidence as Exhibit M-5. 
9, Opportunity was given to the aggrieved workman to cross-examine the witness but he declined. Union did 
not take any step and no accommodation was sought for cross-examination of the management witness on any other 
date. The evidence of Management Witness No. | was accordingly closed. 
10. Mr. S. K. Pandey, union representative advancing his argument on behalf of the workman submitted that the 
workman joined Central Hospital, Kalla on 18.03.2019 on his transfer from Jhanjra Project Colliery. On earlier 
occasion according to NCWA the workman was receiving HRA at the Rate of Rs.525.86/- per month and the same 
would be evident from Exhibit W-6, the Pay slip of March, 2019. It is submitted that HRA was stopped from April, 
2019 which can be gathered from Exhibit W-6/1. It is argued that on his transfer to Central Hospital, Kalla the 
workman applied for allotment of quarters on 31.10.2019 (Exhibit W-1) but no quarters was allotted to him. After 
waiting for a considerable period, the workman again applied for allotment of ‘A’ type quarters to him on 12.06.2020 
(Exhibit W-3). The management of ECL did not consider the prayer, due to which the workman continued to suffer 
and had to make his own arrangement for accommodation for his family members at Asansol. The workman 
thereafter submitted application dated 12.08.2020 (Exhibit W-4) for cancellation of his application for allotment of 
quarters. It is argued that the management neither allotted quarters nor paid any HRA to the workman which is illegal 
and contrary to the provisions of NCWA. 
11. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate, in reply argued that the workman was allotted with Quarters on 26.12.2019 
along with 20 other employees on the basis of decision taken in the Housing Committee meeting held on 17.12.2019 
but Sourav Das did not take possession of the same nor did he refuse. Learned advocate heavily relied upon Exhibit 
M-2, the Office Order dated 26.12.2019 related to allotment of quarters to the employees and submitted that in letter 
dated 21.03.2009 (Exhibit M-5) issued by the General Manager (Admin./Welfare) it was informed that in the 35% 
meeting of Coal India Limited Welfare Board Meeting held on 21.04.2007 it was decided that payment of HRA may 
be allowed in those mines / areas only where there is a shortage of quarters. HRA should not be paid if quarters are 
available, or allotted but are not accepted by the concerned employee. Learned advocate strenuously argued that the 
management cannot act on whims and fancies of the workman who after praying for allotment of quarters did not 
accept the quarters allotted to him but prayed for allotment of ‘A’ type quarters for which he was not entitled. It is 
urged that the workman is not entitled to any HRA. 
12. Having, considered the fact and circumstances of this case it is crystal clear that Sourav Das who had been 
receiving HRA at Jhanjra Project Colliery at the rate of Rs.525.86/- per month till March, 2019 and did not get HRA 
after his joining at Central Hospital, Kalla on 18.03.2019. Undisputedly, the workman for the first time applied for 
allotment of quarters to him on 31.10.2019 (Exhibit M-1/W-1) and within a span of one and a half (112) months a 
Housing Committee Meeting was held on 17.12.2019 and Sourav Das along with 20 other employees were allotted 
quarters according to their designation at Central Hospital, Kalla. It is therefore apparent that quarters were available 
and the same were allotted to the employees on the basis of their prayer. Though the workman did not whisper about 
allotment of quarters to him. In Paragraph No. (7) of the written statement the workman stated that the Office Order 
bearing No. ECL/CHK/Quarter/2019/3162 dated 26.12.2019 (Exhibit M-2) has no application upon the workman. In 
his affidavit-in-chief the workman has outright denied the fact of allotment of quarters in his favour, which is untrue. 
The workman neither raised any dispute regarding type of quarters he is entitled nor did he raise any objection that the 
quarters allotted to him was not habitable due to bad state of repair. The management witness satisfactorily proved the 
issuance of Office Order dated 26.12.2019 as Exhibit M-2, whereby Quarters No. NTD-4/4 was allotted to Sourav 
Das. The workman did not venture to refute such facts during cross-examination of the management witness. On the 
basis of such evidence on record, I hold that the concerned workman is only entitled to HRA for the period from 
April, 2019 to November, 2019 until quarters was allotted to him. Since, the management allotted quarters 
commensurate with the grade of the employee, he cannot refuse the same on a plea that he wanted ‘A’ type quarters. 
On the basis of my above findings, I find that the workman is entitled to HRA only for a period of eight (8) months, 
that is from April, 2019 to November, 2019 at the rate of Rs.525.86/- (Rupees five hundred twenty-five and eighty-six 
paise only) per month. 
Hence, 
ORDERED 

that the Industrial Dispute is allowed in part in favour of Sourav Das. The workman is entitled to House Rent 
Allowance at the rate of Rs.525.86/- (Rupees five hundred twenty-five and eighty-six paise only) per month for a 
period of eight (8) months only, from April, 2019 to November, 2019 from the management of employer company. 
He is not entitled to any HRA thereafter from December, 2019 as he refused to occupy the quarters allotted to him 
without any cogent reason. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to pay the House Rent

14, Now the Authority constituted under Section 41(1) of the Act is an authority with very limited jurisdiction. It can 
only decide in the first appeal whether a termination by the management is valid or not and is within the parameters 
of Section 40 of the Act. The said Authority, in our view, has absolutely no jurisdiction to decide whether a settlement 
entered into under Section 18(1) of the Industrial Disputes Act between the representatives of the Workmen and of the 
Management, is vitiated by undue influence or misrepresentation or coercion on the part of the Management. The 
Authority, namely, the Assistant Commissioner of Labour, was never intended by the A.P. Legislature to have 
jurisdiction to go into the question of the validity of a settlement arrived at under Section 18 of the Industrial Disputes

Act by an Industrial Court. That Parliament has, in fact, constituted Industrial Courts under the Industrial Disputes

Further in the case of Herbertsons Limited Vs. Workmen of Herbertsons Limited and Ors, 1977 AIR 322, 
Hon’ble Supreme Court have held:- 


The Tribunal thought that the question of the quantum of membership of the 2nd Respondent did not call for a finding 
at all in view of Ihis Court's order. As observed above that was not a correct assumption. On the other hand, we feel 
that this view of the Tribunal has led it to approach the matter in an entirely erroneous manner. The Tribunal is, 
rightly enough, conscious that under section 18 (1) of the Industrial Disputes Act the settlement was binding on the 
company and the members of the 3rd Respondent union. Even so, the Tribunal devoted nearly half of its order in 
scanning the evidence given by the company and Respondent No. 3 to find out whether the terms of the settlement had 
been explained by the President of the union to the workmen or not and whether the workers voluntarily accepted the 
settlement knowing all the "consequences". This to our mind is again an entirely wrong approach. 


“When a recognised union negotiates with an employer the workers as individuals do not come into the picture. It is 
not necessary that each individual worker should know the implications of the settlement since a recognised union, 
which is expected to protect the legitimate interests of labour, enters into a settlement in the best interests of labour. 
This would be the normal rule. We cannot altogether rule out exceptional cases where there may be allegations of 
mala fides, fraud or even corruption or other induce- ments. Nothing of that kind has been suggested against the 
President of the 3rd Respondent in this case. That being the position, prima facie, this is a settlement in the course of 
collective bargaining and, therefore, is entitled to due weight and consideration. 


It is not possible to scan the settlement in bits and pieces and hold some parts good and acceptable and others bad. 
Unless it can be demonstrated that the objectionable portion is such that it completely outweighs all the other 
advantages gained the Court will be slow to hold a settle- ment as unfair and unjust. The settlement has to be 
accepted or rejected as a whole and we are unable to reject it as a whole as unfair or unjust. Even before this Court 
the 3rd Respondent representing admittedly the large majority of the workmen has stood by this settlement and that is 
a strong factor which it is difficult to ignore. As stated elsewhere in the judgment, we cannot also be oblivious of the 
fact that all workmen of the company have accepted the settlement. Besides, the period of settlement has since expired 
and we are informed that the employer and the 3rd Respondent are negotiating another settlement with further 
improvements. These factors, apart from what has been stated above, and the need for industrial peace and harmony 
when a union backed by a large majority of workmen has accepted a settlement in the course of collective bargaining 
have impelled us not to interfere with this settlement. That being the position, we unhold the settlement as fair and just 
and order that the award of the Tribunal shall be substituted by the settlement dated October 18, 1973. The said 
settlement shall be the substituted award. The appeal is disposed of accordingly. There will be no order as to costs.”’

(b) the Workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' 
average pay for every completed year of continuous service] or any part thereof in excess of six months; and 


(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government or such authority as may be specified 
by the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette]. 


Compensation to workmen in case of transfer of undertakings. 
Section 25B defines the term continuous service which provides 
Definition of continuous service.- For the purposes of this Chapter,-- 


(1) a Workman shall be said to be in continuous service for a period if he is, for that period, in uninterrupted service, 
including service which may be interrupted on account of sickness or authorized leave or an accident or a strike 
which is not illegal, or a lock- out or a cessation of work which is not due to any fault on the part of the Workman; 


(2) where a Workman is not in continuous service within the meaning of clause (1) for a period of one year or six 
months, he shall be deemed to be in continuous service under an employer-- 


(a) for a period of one year, if the Workman, during a period of twelve calendar months preceding the date with 
reference to which calculation is to be made, has actually worked under the employer for not less than-- 


(i) one hundred and ninety days in the case of a Workman employed below ground in a mine; and 
(ii) two hundred and forty days, in any other case;

In Rajasthan State Ganganagar S. Mills Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan and Anr. (2004) Apex Court held: 


"It was the case of the Workman that he had worked for more than 240 days in the year concerned. This claim was 
denied by the appellant. It was for the claimant to lead evidence to show that he had worked for 240 days in the year 
preceding the date of his termination. He has filed an affidavit. It is statement which is in his favor and that cannot be 
regarded as sufficient evidence for any Court or Tribunal to come to the conclusion that in fact the claimant had 
worked for 240 days in a year These aspects were highlighted in Range Forest Officer v. S.T. Hadimani (2002 (3) 
SCC 25. No proof of receipt of salary or wages for 240 days or order or record in that regard was produced. Mere 
non-production of the muster roll for a particular period was not sufficient for the Labour Court held that the 
Workman had worked for 240 days as claimed." 


In Municipal Corporation, Faridabad v. Siri Niwas (2004 (8) SCC 195), held "the burden was on the Workman to 
show that he was working for more than 240 days in the preceding one year prior to his alleged retrenchment." In 
MP. Electricity Board v. Hariram (2004 (8) SCC 246) the position was again reiterated in paragraph I] as follows: 
"The above burden having not been discharged and the Labour Court having held so, in our opinion, the Industrial 
Court and the High Court erred in basing an order of reinstatement solely on an adverse inference drawn 
erroneously ..”
